rules.label: Sliding Fee Discount Program for income at or below 200% FPL
rules.quote: Sliding fees are specific to all individuals and families with annual incomes at or below 200 percent of the federal poverty line.

eca_not_before.quote: If the patient does not make effort to pay or fails to respond within 60 days, this constitutes refusal to pay.

payment_plan.quote: At this point in time, [Name of Practice] can explore options not limited to, but including offering the patient a payment plan, waiving of charges, or referring for patient collections efforts.

notes: Policy covers emergency or medically necessary care per FAP Covered Providers list; noncovered providers listed separately.
Income definition includes extensive list of sources; noncash benefits (food stamps, housing subsidies) do not count.

Required documentation: prior year W-2, two most recent bank statements, two most recent pay stubs; self-employed submit three months income/expenses; self-declaration only in special circumstances (e.g., homeless).
Self-declared patients responsible for 100% of charges until management determines appropriate category.
Renewal applications required every 12 months or upon financial change; 10 business days to respond to termination notice.

If application cannot be processed due to missing info, applicant has 2 weeks from notification to supply info without application date adjustment; otherwise application re-dated to date info supplied.
Sliding fee schedule updated annually in first quarter with latest federal poverty guidelines.
Determination provided in writing with discount percentage or denial reason; if approved for less than 100% discount or denied, patient must immediately establish payment arrangements.
Reapplication look-back period is lesser of six months or expiration of last application.

Refusal to pay: verbal unwillingness or vacating without paying triggers written notice; if not on sliding fee schedule, application sent with notice; after 60 days no response/effort, collections options explored.
Information stored in shared confidential file in business office.
Policy violations by employees subject to disciplinary action up to termination.
Discounts based on income and family size only, could include HDC program or whichever comes first.
No discrimination on basis of race, color, sex, national origin, disability, religion, age, sexual orientation, or gender identity.
0 may leave out a condition: Policy states 60 days to respond constitutes refusal to pay, but does not explicitly promise no ECA before that period.
